questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A point $P$ moves on $xy$-plane such that $PS+PS'=4$, where $S(K,0)$ and $S'(-K,0)$, then which of the following is not true about the locus of $P$?
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q1
questions.solution: $PS+PS'=4$. $SS'=2|K|$. Locus is an ellipse if $2|K|<4\implies K\in(-2,2)$; line segment if $2|K|=4\implies K=\pm2$; empty set if $2|K|>4\implies K\in(-\infty,-2)\cup(2,\infty)$. Thus all A, B, C are true.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q1

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: $OA$ and $OB$ are two mutually perpendicular chords of $y^2=4ax$, $O$ being the origin. Line $AB$ will always pass through the point
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q2
questions.solution: Let $A(at_1^2,2at_1)$ and $B(at_2^2,2at_2)$. Perpendicular chords $OA\perp OB\implies t_1t_2=-4$. Equation of chord $AB$ reduces to $2(x-4a)-(t_1+t_2)y=0$, which always passes through $(4a,0)$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q2

questions.text: If the three distinct lines $x+2ay+a=0$, $x+3by+b=0$ and $x+4ay+a=0$ are concurrent, then the point $(a,b)$ lies on a
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q3
questions.solution: Intersection of 1st and 3rd lines gives $x=-a, y=0$. Substituting into 2nd line $-a+b=0\implies b=a$, which represents a straight line.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q3

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If a variable line $3x+4y-\lambda=0$ is such that the two circles $x^2+y^2-2x-2y+1=0$ and $x^2+y^2-18x-2y+78=0$ are on its opposite sides, then the set of all values of $\lambda$ is the interval:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q4
questions.solution: Circles have centers $C_1(1,1), R_1=1$ and $C_2(9,1), R_2=2$. For circles to be on opposite sides of $3x+4y-\lambda=0$, $(7-\lambda)(31-\lambda)<0\implies 7<\lambda<31$. Line must not intersect circles: $|7-\lambda|>5$ and $|31-\lambda|>10\implies 12<\lambda<21$, interval $[12,21]$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q4

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The number of rational point(s) (a point $(a,b)$ is rational, if $a$ and $b$ both are rational numbers) on the circumference of a circle having centre $(\pi,e)$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q5
questions.solution: If a circle has two rational points, its perpendicular bisector has rational slope and passes through center $(\pi,e)$, implying a linear rational relation between $\pi$ and $e$, which is impossible. Hence at most one rational point exists.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q5

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If two points $P$ and $Q$ lie on the hyperbola $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{b^2}=1\ (a<b)$, whose centre $C$ be such that $CP$ is perpendicular to $CQ$, then the value of $\dfrac{1}{CP^2}+\dfrac{1}{CQ^2}$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q6
questions.solution: In polar coordinates, $\dfrac{1}{CP^2}=\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{a^2}-\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{b^2}$ and $\dfrac{1}{CQ^2}=\dfrac{\sin^2\theta}{a^2}-\dfrac{\cos^2\theta}{b^2}$. Adding both gives $\dfrac{1}{CP^2}+\dfrac{1}{CQ^2}=\dfrac{1}{a^2}-\dfrac{1}{b^2}$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q6

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: A straight line $L$ through the point $(3,-2)$ is inclined at an angle $60^\circ$ to the line $\sqrt3x+y=1$. If $L$ also intersects the x-axis, then the equation of $L$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q7
questions.solution: Slope of given line is $-\sqrt3$ (inclination $120^\circ$). Inclination of $L$ is $120^\circ\pm60^\circ$. $180^\circ$ is horizontal ($y=-2$, doesn't intersect x-axis). $60^\circ$ has slope $\sqrt3$. Equation through $(3,-2)$: $y-\sqrt3x+2+3\sqrt3=0$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q7

questions.text: The points $A(3,6)$ and $B$ lie on the parabola $y^2=4ax$, such that the chord $AB$ subtends $90^\circ$ at the origin, then the length of the chord $AB$ is equal to
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q8
questions.solution: For $y^2=4ax$, $A(3,6)\implies a=3, t_1=1$. Since $AB$ subtends $90^\circ$ at origin, $t_1t_2=-4\implies t_2=-4\implies B(48,-24)$. Length $AB=\sqrt{45^2+(-30)^2}=15\sqrt{13}$ units.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q8

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Suppose $S$ and $S'$ are foci of the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{25}+\dfrac{y^2}{16}=1$. If $P$ is a variable point on the ellipse and if $\Delta$ is the area (in sq. units) of the triangle $PSS'$, then the maximum value of $\Delta$ is double of
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q9
questions.solution: Foci distance $SS'=2ae=6$. Area $\Delta=\tfrac12(6)|y_P|=3|y_P|$. Maximum $\Delta=3(4)=12$. AM-GM on $\dfrac{3a^3+3b^4}{a^4b^2}\geq3\times2=6$. Max $\Delta=12$ is double of 6.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q9

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Two straight lines having variable slopes $m_1$ and $m_2$ pass through the fixed points $(a,0)$ and $(-a,0)$ respectively. If $m_1m_2=2$, then the eccentricity of the locus of the point of intersection of the lines is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q10
questions.solution: $m_1=\dfrac{y}{x-a}$ and $m_2=\dfrac{y}{x+a}$. $m_1m_2=2\implies \dfrac{y^2}{x^2-a^2}=2\implies \dfrac{x^2}{a^2}-\dfrac{y^2}{2a^2}=1$. Eccentricity $e=\sqrt{1+\dfrac{2a^2}{a^2}}=\sqrt3$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q10

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $L$ be the line passing through the point $P(1,2)$ such that its intercepted segment between the co-ordinate axes is bisected at $P$. If $L_1$ is the line perpendicular to $L$ and passing through the point $(-2,1)$, then the point of intersection of $L$ and $L_1$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q11
questions.solution: Intercepted segment bisected at $(1,2)\implies$ $x$-intercept is $2$, $y$-intercept is $4$. Line $L: 2x+y=4$. Perpendicular line $L_1$ through $(-2,1)$ is $x-2y+4=0$. Intersection is $(4/5,12/5)$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q11

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $(x,y)$ be a variable point on the curve $4x^2+9y^2-8x-36y+15=0$. Then $\min(x^2-2x+y^2-4y+5)+\max(x^2-2x+y^2-4y+5)$ is -
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q12
questions.solution: Ellipse equation $\dfrac{(x-1)^2}{(5/2)^2}+\dfrac{(y-2)^2}{(5/3)^2}=1$. Expression is distance squared from center $(1,2)$, having min $=(5/3)^2=25/9$ and max $=(5/2)^2=25/4$. Sum $=25/9+25/4=325/36$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q12

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The locus of the point $(x,y)$ whose distance from the line $y=2x+2$ is equal to the distance from $(2,0)$, is a parabola with the length of latus rectum same as that of the parabola $y=Kx^2$, then the value of $K$ is equal to
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q13
questions.solution: Distance of focus $(2,0)$ from directrix $2x-y+2=0$ is $2a=\dfrac6{\sqrt5}\implies$ latus rectum $4a=\dfrac{12}{\sqrt5}$. For parabola $y=Kx^2$, latus rectum $=\dfrac1K$. Equating $\dfrac1K=\dfrac{12}{\sqrt5}\implies K=\dfrac{\sqrt5}{12}$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q13

questions.text: The vertices of the triangle $ABC$ are $(2,1)$, $(4,3)$ and $(2,5)$. $D,E,F$ are the mid-points of the sides. The area of the triangle $DEF$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q14
questions.solution: Area of $\triangle ABC=\tfrac12|2(3-5)+4(5-1)+2(1-3)|=4$. Midpoint triangle $\triangle DEF$ has area $\tfrac14\text{Area}(\triangle ABC)=1$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q14

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The equation of a circle with origin as centre and passing through the vertices of an equilateral triangle whose median is of length $3a$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q15
questions.solution: Centroid/circumcenter divides median of length $3a$ in ratio $2:1$, so circumradius $R=2a$. Circle equation is $x^2+y^2=R^2=4a^2$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q15

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Suppose the parabola $(y-k)^2=4(x-h)$, with vertex $A$, passes through $O=(0,0)$ and $L=(0,2)$. Let $D$ be an end point of the latus rectum. Let the y-axis intersect the axis of the parabola at $P$. Then $\angle PDA$ is equal to
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q16
questions.solution: Parabola $(y-1)^2=4(x+1/4)$ has vertex $A(-1/4,1)$, focus $S(3/4,1)$, latus rectum endpoint $D(3/4,3)$, and axis-y-intercept $P(0,1)$. Slopes $m_{DA}=2, m_{DP}=8/3$. $\tan\theta=\left|\dfrac{8/3-2}{1+16/3}\right|=\dfrac2{19}\implies \theta=\tan^{-1}(2/19)$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q16

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: On a rectangular hyperbola $x^2-y^2=a^2, a>0$, three points $A,B,C$ are taken as follows: $A=(-a,0)$; $B$ and $C$ are placed symmetrically with respect to the X-axis on the branch of the hyperbola not containing $A$. Suppose that the $\triangle ABC$ is equilateral. If the side length of the $\triangle ABC$ is $ka$, then $k$ lies in the interval
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q17
questions.solution: Points $B,C$ on hyperbola $x^2-y^2=a^2$ are $(a\sec\theta,\pm a\tan\theta)$. Equilateral triangle $\triangle ABC$ with $A(-a,0)$ gives $a(\sec\theta+1)=\sqrt3a\tan\theta\implies \sec\theta=2\implies \tan\theta=\sqrt3$. Side length $BC=2\sqrt3a\implies k=2\sqrt3\approx3.46\in(2,4]$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q17

questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q18
questions.solution: Point $P(2,1)$ shifted by $5\sqrt2$ along direction angle $135^\circ$ gives $Q(-3,6)$. Reflection of $(-3,6)$ in line $y=-x$ gives $(6,-3)$.

questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q19
questions.solution: For parabola with $a=2$, focal chord distance from vertex $d=a\sin\theta=2\implies \theta=90^\circ$, so the focal chord is the latus rectum of length $4a=8$.

questions.text: The orthocentre of the triangle with vertices $(-2,-6)$, $(-2,4)$ and $(1,3)$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q20
questions.solution: Vertices $A(-2,-6)$ and $B(-2,4)$ form vertical line $x=-2$. Altitude from $C(1,3)$ is $y=3$. Altitude from $A$ to $BC$ (slope $-1/3$) has equation $y=3x$. Intersection of $y=3$ and $y=3x$ is $(1,3)$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $C_1$ be the graph of $xy=1$ and the reflection of $C_1$ in the line $y=2x$ is $C_2$. If the equation of $C_2$ is expressed as $12x^2+bxy+cy^2+d=0$, then the value of $(b+c+d)$ is equal to
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q21
questions.solution: Reflection of $xy=1$ in line $y=2x$: $x'=-3/5x+4/5y, y'=4/5x+3/5y$. Substituting into $xy=1$ gives $12x^2-7xy-12y^2+25=0$. Thus $b=-7,c=-12,d=25$, so $b+c+d=6$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q21

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: The vertices of the triangle $ABC$ are $A(0,0), B(3,0)$ and $C(3,4)$, where $A$ and $C$ are foci of an ellipse and $B$ lies on the ellipse. If the length of the latus rectum of the ellipse is $\dfrac{12}{p}$ units, then the value of $2p$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q22
questions.solution: Foci $A(0,0)$ and $C(3,4)\implies 2ae=5$. Point $B(3,0)$ on ellipse gives $2a=BA+BC=3+4=7\implies a=7/2$. $b^2=a^2(1-e^2)=6$. Latus rectum $=\dfrac{2b^2}{a}=\dfrac{24}{7}=\dfrac{12}{3.5}=\dfrac{12}{p}\implies 2p=7$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q22

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let in $\triangle ABC$ coordinates of vertex $A$ is $(0,0)$. Equation of the internal angle bisector of $\angle ABC$ is $x+y-1=0$ and mid-point of $BC$ is $(1,3)$. The ordinate of vertex $C$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q23
questions.solution: Image of $A(0,0)$ in bisector $x+y-1=0$ is $A'(1,1)$, which lies on line $BC$. Midpoint of $BC$ is $M(1,3)$, so line $BC$ is $x=1$. $B=(1,0)$ on bisector $\implies$ ordinate of $C$ is $y_C=2(3)-0=6$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q23

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: Let $PQ$ be the focal chord of the parabola $y^2=4x$. If the centre of the circle having $PQ$ as its diameter lies on the line $y=\dfrac{-4}{\sqrt5}$, then the length (in units) of chord $PQ$ is $M$, find $10M$
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q24
questions.solution: Focal chord $PQ$ of $y^2=4x$ has midpoint $y_c=t-1/t=-4/\sqrt5$. Length $PQ=(t-1/t)^2+4=16/5+4=36/5=7.2\implies 10M=72$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q24

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.text: If the circle $(x-a)^2+y^2=25$ intersects the circle $x^2+(y-b)^2=16$ in such a way that the length of the common chord is $8$ units, then the value of $a^2+b^2$ is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics answer key · Q25
questions.solution: Common chord length $8$ equals diameter of smaller circle $R_2=4$. Centre distance $C_1C_2=\sqrt{R_1^2-R_2^2}=\sqrt{25-16}=3\implies a^2+b^2=3^2=9$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Mathematics solution · Q25

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: There is a horizontal film of soap solution. On it a thread is placed in the form of a loop. The film is pierced inside the loop and the thread becomes a circular loop of radius $R$. If the surface tension of the film be $T$, then tension in the thread will be:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q1
questions.solution: Consider a small thread element subtending angle $d\theta$ at the center. The outward force due to surface tension is $2T(Rd\theta)$ since soap film has two surfaces. The inward restoring force due to thread tension is $2T_{thread}\sin(d\theta/2)\approx T_{thread}d\theta$. Balancing forces gives $T_{thread}d\theta = 2TRd\theta \implies T_{thread}=2RT$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q1

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle executing SHM has a maximum speed of $0.5\ \text{m s}^{-1}$ and a maximum acceleration of $1.0\ \text{m s}^{-2}$. The angular frequency of oscillation is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q2
questions.solution: In SHM, $v_{max}=A\omega$ and $a_{max}=A\omega^2$. Dividing the two expressions gives $\omega=\dfrac{a_{max}}{v_{max}}=\dfrac{1.0}{0.5}=2\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q2

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Consider two stress-strain graphs of two metal wires of different materials (say material X and Y). Here, A, B, C and D represent the proportionality limit point, yield point, ultimate strength point and breaking point. Which of the following statement is correct?
options: Wire X is more ductile than wire Y.
Wire Y is more ductile than wire X.
Young's modulus of wire X is more than wire Y.
These wires cannot be compared as data is insufficient.
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q3
questions.solution: The ductility of a material is determined by the length of the plastic deformation region between the yield point/ultimate strength and the breaking point. Wire X has a wider region between C and D than wire Y, making wire X more ductile.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q3

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A given shaped glass tube having uniform cross section is filled with water and is mounted on a rotatable shaft as shown in figure. If the tube is rotated with a constant angular velocity $\omega$ then
options: water levels in both sections A and B go up
water level in section A goes up and that in B comes down
water level in section A comes down and that in B it goes up
water levels remain same in both sections.
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q4
questions.solution: When rotated with angular velocity $\omega$, pressure increases radially as $\Delta P=\tfrac12\rho\omega^2 r^2$. Section B is at distance $2L$ from the axis while section A is at distance $L$, so higher pressure is exerted towards B, causing the water level in section A to come down and in section B to go up.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q4

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Eight equal drops of water are falling through air with a steady velocity of $10\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$. If the drops combine to form a single drop of big size, then the terminal velocity of this big drop is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q5
questions.solution: Terminal velocity $v_T\propto r^2$. Volume conservation $8\times\tfrac43\pi r^3=\tfrac43\pi R^3 \implies R=2r$. New terminal velocity $v_T'=(R/r)^2 v_T=2^2\times10=40\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q5

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The position and velocity of a particle executing simple harmonic motion at $t=0$ are given by $3$ cm and $8\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$ respectively. If the angular frequency of the particle is $2\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$, then the amplitude of oscillation (in cm) is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q6
questions.solution: Using $v=\omega\sqrt{A^2-x^2}$, substitute $v=8\ \text{cm s}^{-1}$, $x=3$ cm, and $\omega=2\ \text{rad s}^{-1}$: $8=2\sqrt{A^2-9}\implies 4=\sqrt{A^2-9}\implies 16=A^2-9\implies A=5$ cm.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q6

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text:
Two wires of same material are hanging as shown in the figure. Breaking stress is equal for both the wires.

Assertion: If mass $m_1$ increases, then upper wire will break first.
Reason: Breaking load of two wires of same material can be different.
options: Assertion is true, reason is true; reason is a correct explanation for assertion.
Assertion is true, reason is true; reason is not a correct explanation for assertion.
Assertion is true, reason is false.
Assertion is false but, reason is true.
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q7
questions.solution: Tension in the upper wire is $T_1=(m_1+m_2)g$ while tension in the lower wire is $T_2=m_2g$. Increasing $m_1$ increases stress in the upper wire, making it break first (Assertion true). Breaking load depends on area of cross section (Reason true), but this does not explain why $m_1$ specifically increases tension in the upper wire.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q7

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: Water enters through end A with speed $v_A$ and leaves through end B with speed $v_B$ of a cylindrical tube AB. The tube is always completely filled with water. In case I, the tube is horizontal and in case II, it is vertical with end A upwards and in case III, it is vertical with end B upwards. We have $v_A=v_B$ for
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q8
questions.solution: By the equation of continuity $A_Av_A=A_Bv_B$, for an incompressible liquid in a tube of uniform cross-section $(A_A=A_B)$, $v_A=v_B$ in all orientations (horizontal or vertical).
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q8

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle is dropped from depth of $20$ m below the earth's surface along a tunnel created inside the planet of mass $M$ with radius $R$ as shown in the figure, the time period of oscillation is: (if $GM=10R^3$, given $\pi^2=10$)
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q9
questions.solution: Inside a uniform spherical planet, gravitational force inside a tunnel is linear with distance from center $r$, $F=-\dfrac{GMm}{R^3}r$. The time period of SHM is $T=2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{R^3}{GM}}$. Given $GM=10R^3\implies \dfrac{GM}{R^3}=10$, so $T=\dfrac{2\pi}{\sqrt{10}}$. With $\pi^2=10$, $T=\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}}{\sqrt{10}}=2$ s.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q9

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: In a cylinder-piston arrangement, the air is under a pressure $P_1$. A soap bubble of radius $r$ lies inside the cylinder. Soap bubble has surface tension $T$. The radius of soap bubble is to be reduced to half. Find the pressure $P_2$ to which air should be compressed isothermally.
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q10
questions.solution: Initial pressure inside soap bubble $P_{in,1}=P_1+\dfrac{4T}{r}$. When radius halves to $r/2$, final inside pressure $P_{in,2}=P_2+\dfrac{4T}{r/2}=P_2+\dfrac{8T}{r}$. For isothermal process, $P_{in,1}V_1=P_{in,2}V_2 \implies \left(P_1+\dfrac{4T}{r}\right)V=\left(P_2+\dfrac{8T}{r}\right)\dfrac{V}{8}\implies P_2=8P_1+\dfrac{24T}{r}$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q10

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The edge of an aluminium cube is $10$ cm long. One face of the cube is firmly fixed to a vertical wall. A mass of $100$ kg is then attached to the opposite face of the cube. The shear modulus of aluminium is $25$ GPa. What is the vertical deflection of this face?
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q11
questions.solution: Shear stress $=\dfrac{F}{A}=\eta\dfrac{\Delta x}{L}\implies \Delta x=\dfrac{FL}{A\eta}=\dfrac{mgL}{L^2\eta}=\dfrac{mg}{L\eta}$. Substituting values: $\Delta x=\dfrac{100\times9.8}{0.1\times25\times10^9}=3.92\times10^{-7}$ m.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q11

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: A particle starts SHM from the mean position. Its amplitude is $a$ and total energy $E$. At one instant its kinetic energy is $3E/4$. Its displacement at that instant is
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q12
questions.solution: Total energy $E=KE+PE$. Given $KE=\tfrac34E$, $PE=E-\tfrac34E=\tfrac{E}{4}$. Since $PE=\tfrac12m\omega^2x^2$ and $E=\tfrac12m\omega^2a^2$, $\dfrac{x^2}{a^2}=\dfrac14 \implies x=\dfrac{a}{2}$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q12

questions.subject: Physics
questions.text: The Young's modulus of steel is twice that of brass. Two wires of same length and of same area of cross-section, one of steel and another of brass, are suspended from the same roof. If we want the lower ends of the wires to be at the same level, then the weights added to the steel and brass wires must be in the ratio of:
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q13
questions.solution: Elongation $\Delta L=\dfrac{WL}{AY}$. For lower ends to remain at the same level, $\Delta L_{steel}=\Delta L_{brass}\implies \dfrac{W_{steel}}{Y_{steel}}=\dfrac{W_{brass}}{Y_{brass}}\implies \dfrac{W_{steel}}{W_{brass}}=\dfrac{Y_{steel}}{Y_{brass}}=2:1$.
questions.solutionSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics solution · Q13

questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q14

options: First increase and then decrease to the original value
First decrease and then increase to the original value

questions.solution: As water flows out, the center of gravity of the bob shifts downwards, increasing the effective length $L$ of the pendulum and thus increasing the time period $T$. questions.solution: Bulk modulus $B=\dfrac{p}{(-\Delta V/V)}\implies \dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=\dfrac{p}{B}$. For a sphere, $V=\tfrac43\pi r^3\implies \dfrac{\Delta V}{V}=3\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}$. Thus fractional decrease in radius $\dfrac{\Delta r}{r}=\dfrac{p}{3B}$.

questions.text: The displacement of a particle is given at time $t$ by: $x=A\sin(2\omega t)+B\sin^2(\omega t)$. Then,
options: the motion of the particle is SHM with an amplitude of $\sqrt{A^2+\dfrac{B^2}{4}}$
the motion of the particle is not SHM, but oscillatory with a time period of $T=\pi/\omega$
the motion of the particle is oscillatory with a time period of $T=\pi/2\omega$

questions.text: Two springs with negligible masses and force constants $k_1=200\ \text{N/m}$ and $k_2=160\ \text{N/m}$ are attached to the block of mass $m=10\ \text{kg}$ as shown in figure (frictionless). Initially the block is at rest, at the equilibrium position in which both springs are neither stretched nor compressed. At time $t=0$, sharp impulse of $50\ \text{N s}$ is given to the block with a hammer along the spring. Then the amplitude of spring will be $K$ metre. Find $6K$
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Physics answer key · Q22
questions.solution: Equivalent spring constant for parallel springs $k_{eq}=k_1+k_2=200+160=360\ \text{N/m}$. Velocity after impulse $v_0=J/m=50/10=5\ \text{m/s}$. Energy conservation $\tfrac12k_{eq}A^2=\tfrac12mv_0^2 \implies 360A^2=10(25)=250 \implies A=\dfrac{5}{6}$ m. Thus $6K=6\times(5/6)=5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: The reaction, cis Z $\underset{K_b}{\overset{K_f}{\rightleftharpoons}}$ trans Z is first order in both directions. At $28^\circ$C, the equilibrium constant is $10^{-2}$ and the rate constant $k_f=3\times10^{-5}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. In an experiment starting with the pure cis-form, how long would it take for half of the equilibrium amount of trans-isomer to be formed?
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Chemistry answer key · Q4
questions.solution: Equilibrium constant $K=\dfrac{k_f}{k_b}=10^{-2}\implies k_b=\dfrac{3\times10^{-5}}{10^{-2}}=3\times10^{-3}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. Overall rate constant $k_{overall}=k_f+k_b=3.03\times10^{-3}\ \text{s}^{-1}$. Time to reach half equilibrium amount $t=\dfrac{\ln 2}{k_{overall}}=\dfrac{0.693}{3.03\times10^{-3}}\approx2.3\times10^2$ s.

questions.text: The voltage of the cell consisting of $Li(s)$ and $F_2(g)$ electrodes is $5.92$ V at standard condition at $298$ K. What is the voltage if the electrolyte consists of $2$M $LiF$? ($\ln2=0.693$, $R=8.314\ \text{J K}^{-1}\text{mol}^{-1}$ and $F=96500\ \text{C mol}^{-1}$)

$NO_3(g)+NO_2(g)\xrightarrow{fast}N_2O_5(g)$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.text: A current of $2.0$ A when passed for $5$ hours through a molten metal salt deposits $22.2$ g of metal of atomic weight $177$. The oxidation state of the metal in the metal salt is (integer only without $+$ or $-$)
questions.answerSource: Supplied QPT 4 HTML · Chemistry answer key · Q25
questions.solution: $Q=It=2.0\times18000=36000$ C $=0.373$ mol $e^-$. Moles of metal $=\dfrac{22.2}{177}=0.1254$ mol. Oxidation state $=\dfrac{0.373}{0.1254}\approx3$.
